data.name: England
data.gender_notes: England is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Originating from the Old English word 'Englisc', meaning 'English', this name refers to the land inhabited by the Angles, a Germanic tribe. The name England symbolizes the heritage and history of the English people. The name England carries the meaning “The land of the Angles” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose England usually hope their child will grow to embody the land of the angles and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Connection to ancient Germanic roots and culture
data.etymology: England belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “The land of the Angles.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of England total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: England represents the rich history and identity of the English people and their Anglo-Saxon heritage. It is a term that conjures images of monarchs, castles, and lush landscapes, as well as a strong cultural continuity that has endured through the ages. England's influence can be seen in its contributions to literature, art, science, and language, making it a crucial piece of the collective cultural memory of the world.
data.spiritual_significance: England holds a special place in the spiritual realm for Christians, as it was the birthplace of the Anglican Church, an important branch of Christianity. The Church of England, derived from the older English traditional faith, is a significant depository of Christian traditions and beliefs. Furthermore, England's Christian heritage is reflected in its numerous cathedrals, abbeys, and churches, which stand as sacred testaments to the faith and piety of its people.
